explainBack.question: Why doesn't installing the Gemini Windows app mean Gemini can automatically see my screen, files or email?
explainBack.answer: Because the app only changes the route into the same online service. Gemini still receives only what you explicitly give it: text you paste, an image you choose to upload, or Google apps like Gmail and Drive that you deliberately connect. On a work or school account, an administrator additionally gates whether the app works at all — so installation alone grants no new access to your content.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P004 (same shop, new door), P006 (uploads and connections are chosen), P005 (admin enablement), P008 (explicit denial of automatic screen/file access).
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this causal answer; the mechanism of opt-in sharing and admin gating is stated, not merely implied.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A colleague who uses a browser-based AI writing assistant at work installs its new desktop app and worries that the app can now index and read all documents on her laptop, so she considers deleting sensitive files first.
unseenTransfer.question: Using this article's mechanism, does the desktop version change what the assistant can access, and what should she actually check?
unseenTransfer.answer: No — a desktop app changes the route into the tool, not its permissions. The assistant still only sees what she pastes, uploads or explicitly connects, and on a company-managed account her IT administrator controls whether and how it is enabled. Instead of deleting files, she should check which account the app is signed into, review any connection prompts before accepting them, and share only material she is comfortable sending to the service.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The route-vs-tool model (P004, P009), opt-in uploads and connections (P006), and administrator control on managed accounts (P005).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this new situation completely; the transfer requires no facts beyond what the article teaches.
